profile.name: Sam Rivera
profile.subline: Fully remote data and analytics roles for a 2026 graduate · Tailored to your September 2026 resume
profile.stack: SQL, Tableau, Excel, Python, Google Sheets
profile.summary: You have two strengths that most 2026 analytics grads do not: two years of real operations experience and paying clients for your dashboard work. Lead with the freelance business, because it proves delivery without supervision, which is the main thing remote employers screen for. Since you want remote only, the Utah half of this board is shown as needing relocation rather than removed.
profile.applyNow: **Stripe New Grad Software Engineer** and **Capital One's Technology Development Program** are the live board roles that hire remotely; both are a stretch for an analytics profile, so lead with the remote-native employers in the suggested list.
profile.watchLater: Snowflake, Datadog and Okta all post remote analyst reqs in the September-to-November window.

suggested.name: GitLab
suggested.why: **All-remote by design, not by concession.** GitLab has run fully distributed since founding, so a candidate with no fixed metro is not an exception here; your freelance dashboard work also shows you can operate without supervision.
suggested.note: Hires globally into data and analytics roles; search 'Data Analyst' and look for their entry-level 'Associate' postings on about.gitlab.com/jobs.

suggested.name: Zapier
suggested.why: **Fully distributed with a strong analytics function.** Automation is their product, and your operations-coordinator background plus Tableau work reads as someone who automates their own job.
suggested.note: All roles are remote; check zapier.com/jobs and search 'Data Analyst' and 'Analytics'.

suggested.name: Automattic
suggested.why: **One of the oldest all-remote companies.** Hiring is project-based rather than program-based, which suits a candidate whose strongest evidence is a portfolio.
suggested.note: Applies through automattic.com/work-with-us; expect a paid trial project rather than a standard interview loop.

suggested.name: Coinbase
suggested.why: **Remote-first fintech.** Their analytics teams hire entry-level, and crypto data work is unusually SQL-heavy, which plays to your strength.
suggested.note: Officially remote-first; search coinbase.com/careers for 'Data Analyst' and 'Associate'.

suggested.name: Dropbox
suggested.why: **Virtual First policy makes remote the default.** Fewer entry-level analytics seats than the bigger names, so apply early when they open.
suggested.note: Their Virtual First policy covers most roles; watch dropbox.com/jobs for analyst openings.

suggested.name: Atlassian
suggested.why: **TEAM Anywhere means location genuinely does not gate hiring.** Their data roles want SQL plus a dashboarding tool, which is exactly your stack.
suggested.note: Runs a graduate program plus rolling analyst roles; search atlassian.com/company/careers for 'Data Analyst'.

suggested.name: Twilio
suggested.why: **Remote-first since 2020.** Analytics roles here sit close to customer data, which suits an operations background.
suggested.note: Search twilio.com/company/jobs for 'Analyst'; most postings list remote eligibility by country.

suggested.name: DuckDuckGo
suggested.why: **Fully remote and deliberately small.** Very few openings, so this is a watch-and-pounce employer rather than a reliable application.
suggested.note: All roles remote; check duckduckgo.com/hiring occasionally.

suggested.name: Remote.com
suggested.why: **A company whose product is remote employment.** Entry-level analytics openings appear irregularly but the culture fit argument writes itself.
suggested.note: Search remote.com/careers for 'Analyst'; hiring is global.

suggested.name: Toptal
suggested.why: **Fully distributed, and a plausible bridge from freelancing.** Your existing Tableau client work is directly relevant to how they staff projects.
suggested.note: Both internal roles and network placement are remote; start at toptal.com/careers.
